chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:

Whoever takes account of his self is benefited, and whoever remains neglectful of it suffers. Whoever fears remains safe; whoever takes instruction (from things around) perceives; and whoever perceives gains understanding, and whoever gains understanding secures knowledge.

key_terms.حَاسَبَ: took account of / held to account

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of self-accountability and observation in Shia ethics?
ai.summary: This hadith encapsulates the Shia concept of *muhasabah* (self-accountability) as the cornerstone of spiritual growth, linking it to the intellectual journey from *ibrah* (taking lessons) to *ilm* (true knowledge). It reflects the epistemological framework where fear of God (*khawf*) acts as a'mal*) serves as the catalyst for safety from divine punishment, while keen observation leads to deep understanding. This chain underscores the integration of introspection and intellectual clarity in achieving spiritual success.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 208. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:

Whoever takes account of his self is benefited, and whoever remains neglectful of it suffers. Whoever fears remains safe; whoever takes instruction (from things around) perceives; and whoever perceives gains understanding, and whoever gains understanding secures knowledge.
